result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
I approved 2 of the 3 pending work orders and left 1 pending; none were cancelled. The gas-classification tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I classified the sample by hand using the IEC 60599 ratios.

**Pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1 (MAIN)**
| WO | Description | Priority | Reported | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04 UTC | none |
| 1000052 | Confirmatory DGA oil sample (worst-case TDCG forecast, IEEE C57.104 Condition 4) | 1 | 2026-09-30 22:17 UTC | none |
| 1000053 | Outage + inspection, 2024-01-20..21 (C57.104 Cond 4) | 1 | 2026-09-30 22:19 UTC | none |

**Latest oil sample (2024-01-19):** H₂ 2850, CH₄ 7400, C₂H₆ 5470, C₂H₄ 16650, C₂H₂ 7, CO 32 ppm. All five fault gases are present, so the classification is reliable.
- **Ratios:** C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 0.0004 (below 0.1), CH₄/H₂ = 2.60 (above 1), C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 3.04 (between 1 and 4).
- **Fault type:** IEC 60599 classes this as **T2, a thermal fault in oil at 300–700 °C**. The Rogers code (0-2-2) and the Duval triangle (69% C₂H₄) point to the hotter band, above 700 °C. Either way it is a thermal fault with no sign of arcing or discharge.
- **Paper involvement:** CO is only 32 ppm, so the paper insulation is not significantly involved.
- **Acetylene:** 7 ppm, which is above the 1 ppm trigger.

**Outcomes**
| WO | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | **Approved**; priority stays 1 (already 1, so no change needed) | Glowing or coked tap-changer contacts are one of IEC 60599's listed examples of a T2 thermal fault, which matches the gases. It is tap changer work and acetylene is 7 ppm, above 1 ppm. |
| 1000052 | **Approved**; priority unchanged at 1 | It is a routine oil sampling job, and no other open work order covers sampling. The 2024-01-19 sample may already be the confirmatory sample it asks for, so check before sending someone out. |
| 1000053 | **Left pending** | Its description is a general outage and inspection triggered by the total gas level (Condition 4), not the specific thermal fault, and it complements 1000051 rather than duplicating it. |

details.suggestions: The agent pulled the correct asset/site, retrieved the latest DGA reading (all five fault gases present plus CO), approved 1000051 and 1000052 (confirmed APPR in tool output), left 1000053 pending with a one-sentence reason, and produced the requested outcome table. Its manual IEC 60599 classification (T2 thermal, no paper involvement, C2H2 7 ppm > 1 ppm) is arithmetically correct and the outcomes are consistent with the rules. However, several expected steps were not carried out: fmsr.interpret_dga failed twice ('LLM unavailable') and the agent substituted a hand calculation rather than obtaining a tool-based classification, and it never passed co to the tool; wo.get_workorder was not called for per-WO details; no explicit wo.list_workorders(status=OPEN) call was made to check for duplicates (the single unfiltered list call's output is recorded as null, so the duplicate check and the existence/details of 1000053 cannot be verified from the trace). To fully meet the expected behavior, the agent should list pending-approval and open WOs separately, fetch each WO with get_workorder, retry or clearly flag the interpret_dga failure as a limitation on the classification's reliability, and explicitly document the duplicate check result for each WO.
